steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Grow PDCLs for ≥48 h undisturbed; resuspend all ATAC‑seq adapters to a 25 µM working stock; prepare fresh ATAC‑seq lysis buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 % IGEPAL); pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C and set the thermal mixer to 37 °C; have Nextera TD buffer, TDE1 transposase, nuclease‑free water, ice‑cold PBS, Qiagen MiniElute PCR kit, and DNase‑free water ready.

steps.title: Harvest and count cells
steps.instruction: Trypsinize adherent PDCLs, collect the suspension, and count cells; pipette the cells with a 200 µL tip to obtain a homogeneous single‑cell suspension; aim for 100 000 cells per reaction (optimize cell‑to‑transposase ratio if needed).

steps.title: Wash and lyse cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 000 cells to a tube, centrifuge 5 min at 600 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant, add 50 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge again 5 min at 600 × g, 4 °C and discard supernatant; add 50 µL ice‑cold ATAC‑seq lysis buffer, gently dislodge the pellet, and centrifuge immediately 10 min at 600 × g, 4 °C; keep the pellet on ice and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Make transposition master mix
steps.instruction: While the lysed pellet is spinning, combine 25 µL TD (2× Nextera reaction buffer), 4.7 µL TDE1 (Nextera Tn5 transposase), and 22.3 µL nuclease‑free H₂O to form the transposition reaction mix.

steps.title: Perform transposition reaction
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in the 52 µL transposition mix, then incubate at 37 °C for 30 min with shaking at 400 rpm on an Eppendorf thermal mixer.

steps.title: Purify transposed DNA
steps.instruction: Immediately after incubation, purify the DNA using the Qiagen MiniElute PCR purification kit and elute the purified DNA in 10 µL DNase‑free water.

steps.title: Store purified DNA (optional)
steps.instruction: If not proceeding directly to library preparation, store the eluted DNA at –20 °C for up to 72 h.

steps.title: Create sample sheet for analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare a CSV/XLSX (or R data frame) containing sample ID, condition, replicate (if any), path to the BAM file, and path to the MACS2 peak file for each library.

steps.title: Load peaks with DiffBind
steps.instruction: Load the DiffBind library in R and read the sample sheet with dba() to create a DiffBind object containing all peaksets.

steps.title: Identify condition‑specific peaks
steps.instruction: Use dba.count() and dba.contrast() (or equivalent) on the DiffBind object, setting the peak ‘size’ parameter to 200 bp to focus motif detection around peak centers.

steps.title: Find motifs with HOMER
steps.instruction: Run HOMER’s findMotifsGenome.pl on the condition‑specific peak BED file, comparing against a random background (or user‑provided background) to identify enriched transcription‑factor motifs.

steps.title: Annotate peaks with ChIPseeker
steps.instruction: Load ChIPseeker, TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene, and org.Hs.eg.db in R; then call annotatePeak(dba.report.object, tssRegion=c(-3000,3000), TxDb=txdb, annoDb="org.Hs.eg.db") to map peaks to genomic features.

steps.title: Subset distal intergenic peaks
steps.instruction: From the annotatedPeak object, extract peaks where annotation == "Distal Intergenic" (e.g., distalPeaks <- subset(annotatedPeakList@anno, annotation=="Distal Intergenic")).

steps.title: Run KEGG and Reactome enrichment
steps.instruction: Load ReactomePA, clusterProfiler, and org.Hs.eg.db; then execute enrichKEGG(gene=as.data.frame(distalPeaks)$geneId, organism='hsa') and enrichPathway(gene=as.data.frame(distalPeaks)$geneId); visualize results with dotplot(..., showCategory=30).
